title: [Collective volume with mostly Sufi texts in Malay, Arabic (and some Sundanese, inside the bindings) Qur’an, surat al-Fatiha ; and other texts] Or. 1332
shelf_note: Malay (Jawi) Sufi texts of Shams al-Din al-Sumatrani, Pasai 1629-30: Sumatran Malay, part of the archipelago Islamic tradition the shelf covers.
structure_note: Every record is an unsplit two-page opening (I3), so each 'page' carries two manuscript pages; the OCR reads right page then left, which works on plain text openings and fails on the diagram openings. Page 1 is the closed binding (spine labels '160', 'Or. 1332') and is 'translated'. The pencil folios on the images (12 on rec 12, 21 on rec 25) show record numbers and folio numbers diverge; the 1 backstep / 2 repeats are most likely misread pencil numerals on openings. Record 12's image is served from the Leiden IIIF URL, not the archived copy, unlike the other records.

reader_summary: A seventeenth-century Malay (Jawi) collection of Shams al-Din al-Sumatrani's Sufi treatises on the martabat and divine attributes. Plain prose openings are transcribed roughly and translated readably, but the colophon's title is misread and the English replaces it with an invented one, and the diagram openings are only partly transcribed, with repeated and templated blocks translated as doctrine. The English cannot be trusted for citation.
book_verdict: An important early Malay Sufi manuscript, but the AI layer fails on its most distinctive pages (diagrams) and misnames the work in the colophon; not fit to show a scholar.

title: [Juzʾ (part) of Qurʾān; from Java] Or. 7092
shelf_note: A Javanese Qur'an manuscript on dluwang-like paper; belongs on a Javanese/Indonesian shelf.
structure_note: Every record is an unsplit opening (I3) with both pages transcribed in reading order. The pencil numbers on the images equal the record numbers (14, 19, 68); the OCR tag read '68' as '48' on record 68, so the 5 printed backsteps are likely misread pencil numerals. 76 of 78 records have OCR and 74 are translated.

reader_summary: A provincial Javanese Qur'an manuscript (parts of al-Baqara, al-Ma'ida, al-An'am). The transcription follows the leaves line by line but normalises the scribe's spelling to the printed Cairo text and once replaces a scribal variant with the standard reading; the English is a sound standard Qur'an translation. One page carries 25 verses recited from memory in a continuation note.
book_verdict: Accurate on the verses that are on the page, but the OCR erases exactly what a manuscript scholar would look for (orthography, variants) and one translation pane carries a long block of memorised text that is not on the leaf; show with a caveat about normalisation.

title: [Wird. A collection of Awrād for the seven days of 7 days of the week. With Malay titles] Or. 7191
shelf_note: Arabic litanies with Malay rubrics ('اين ورد دبچا فد هاري جمعة', this wird is read on Friday), dated 1879: an archipelago devotional manuscript.
structure_note: Unsplit openings (I3), both pages transcribed in order, with catchwords correctly identified. Counts are consistent (35/35/35). Nothing stands out.

reader_summary: A small illuminated 1879 collection of daily litanies (awrad) made of Qur'anic verses, with Malay rubrics telling the reader which day each is recited. The transcription matches the leaves word for word, including the marginal correction and catchwords, and the English is a correct Qur'an translation with verse references. The Malay rubric is slightly misread on one page.
book_verdict: Clean and faithful on every sampled page; a good book to open in front of a scholar.

title: Muqaddimah fi ʿilm al-ʿArabiyah (mutammimah) li masāʾil al-ajrrūmiyah Or. 8471
shelf_note: Al-Hattab's Mutammimat al-Ajurrumiyya, a standard pesantren grammar; the archipelago link rests on provenance (Snouck Hurgronje bequest, 1936) rather than on anything visible on these leaves.
structure_note: Unsplit openings (I3). Record 31, the last, is a pastedown with the Leiden stamp and the 'Legaat Snouck Hurgronje 1936' label plus a blank flyleaf; the OCR tags it Dutch / frontispiece and it is translated. The pencil folios (6, 7, 17) are offset 3 from record numbers; fine.

reader_summary: A nineteenth-century copy of al-Hattab's Mutammimat al-Ajurrumiyya, the advanced Ajurrumiyya grammar used in Southeast Asian Islamic schools. Most lines are transcribed correctly and the English is a clear grammatical translation, but on two of four pages the OCR garbles or replaces a phrase, once inventing a rule the author did not write and once supplying a clause from the standard text that this copy lacks.
book_verdict: Usable as a reading aid with a warning that the transcription sometimes substitutes the standard text or garbles examples; one clean showcase page.
